gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-cairo: Cairo opens a wide channel into every bowl, giving body text a roomy, modern feel beside Red Hat Display's blunt marker-tip heading. Together the sans and the heading make a bold, friendly match.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-cambay: Red Hat Display draws each stroke without any taper where lines meet or end, like a round-tipped marker. Cambay, a plain sans, brings rounds that gap open like a cracked bangle.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-cantarell: Cantarell reads approachable, its c tips pulled well apart. Red Hat Display adds a bold marker line above, and the arches of Cantarell's r, n and m keep up.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-catamaran: Red Hat Display gives its crossbars the same heft as its stems, so every letter looks drawn with one marker. Catamaran, a plain sans, loosens things with curvy, unclamped letters below.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-chiron-hei-hk: Marker-bold and sunlit, Red Hat Display draws true monoline letters with daylight inside every curve. Chiron Hei HK follows as sans-serif text, its wide-open c like a bracelet pulled apart.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-commissioner: Commissioner gives a smooth read with no clogged curves, each stroke drawn at one thickness. Red Hat Display sits above it as a marker-like heading, and the sans keeps the page flowing.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-didact-gothic: Bold marker lines, open curves. Didact Gothic, a sans, never snags on a closed-up bowl, so beneath Red Hat Display's heading the text keeps moving with each stroke carrying equal visual weight.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-dotgothic16: Red Hat Display leads with a marker-like line. DotGothic16, a sans-serif, adds wide channels into each counter and a tube-like thickness that holds through every bend, which is where this pair is strongest.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-doto: Red Hat Display draws its strokes like thin plastic tubing bent into loops, bold yet contemporary. Doto, a sans-serif, gives each glyph wide margins and generous mouths on its rounds.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-el-messiri: One fixed nib width runs through Red Hat Display, which makes the heading bold and marker-like. El Messiri, a sans-serif, does its best work in modest contrast you only notice up close.
